candidates: Avoid unnecessary intermediate variable aliases: if a callback parameter is immediately re-bound (e.g., `forEach(function(_id) { let id = _id; ... })`), rename the parameter directly; if a destructuring assignment uses a rename alias that is immediately reassigned (e.g., `const { nodeList: nl } = uniq(...); nodeList = nl;`), destructure into the final name directly (`const { nodeList } = uniq(...)`). Flag either pattern during review and suggest the simpler form.

When a JS-to-TS refactor rewrites a guard clause condition (e.g., changing `if (value !== undefined) { ... }` to `if (value === undefined) { return; }`), verify that the rewritten check preserves the original runtime behavior for all edge-case inputs—such as empty strings, `null`, and `0`—especially when the TypeScript type annotation may not accurately reflect all values that can arrive at runtime from parser-generated or loosely-typed call sites.
